what: Nomura is Japan's largest investment bank and brokerage. It serves Japanese retail investors through a nationwide branch network, manages assets, and runs a global wholesale business in trading and investment banking.
customers: Japanese individual investors, Japanese and international corporations, and institutional investors worldwide.
money: global trading, investment banking and advisory
brokerage and wealth advice to Japanese households
moat: A retail branch network and brand trusted by Japanese savers, in a country where a very large pool of household cash is slowly moving into investments.
risks: Trading revenue is volatile and consumes capital
Its overseas wholesale business has been loss-making in past years
Only one analyst covers it in this data
opportunities: Japanese households are shifting savings from cash into investments, helped by tax-free investment accounts
Rising Japanese interest rates revive bond trading activity
Net margin of 8% with a growing asset management business
watch: Wholesale division profitability and retail client asset inflows.
